Retrieved 2026-11-06
License MIT, included in fluid-LICENSE.txt and at the top of fluid-solver.js.

The vendored fluid-solver.js retains the upstream GPU simulation passes
(advection, curl, vorticity confinement, divergence, pressure projection and
splat injection), framebuffer management, and shader setup.

Site-specific modifications
- Exported createFluid(canvas) with explicit step, render, resize and dispose.
- Removed promotions, analytics, GUI, screenshots, external images and global inputs.
- Removed bloom, sunrays and unused presentation shaders.
- Converted luminous color display to transparent, premultiplied dark ink.
- Added failed-context/texture/shader checks and GPU resource cleanup.
- Reduced mobile simulation resolution and limited pixel ratio.
- Added a pressure-sensitive retained pigment field, bristle gaps and wet movement.
- Brush pigment and ambient fluid are composited in the same shader, with
  independently retained writing opacity so the writing can remain unchanged.
- Added a clear operation for wet pigment, held pigment, velocity and pressure.
- Added setWritingFlow and stepWriting with an independent, normalized fading
  interval. The InkScene wrapper now defaults to heavy water (0.8/second decay),
  offers light water (0.12/second decay) and still water (no writing decay), and
  removes opacity below 1/255. Switching modes preserves surviving opacity.
  Legacy holdSeconds arguments no longer delay fading. Written pigment is never
  released into ambient dye, so that dye cannot leave uncontrolled writing ghosts.
- Added an optional short-edge-relative Gaussian splat radius, allowing three
  richer broad ambient cloud groups as the initial composition. One moving
  source now continuously adds frame-scaled ink and current rather than periodic
  multi-point bursts. Fixed emission rates and existing dye dissipation keep
  density bounded; heavy/light/still modes change current and drift strength.
- Added shared-brush mask deposit: the exact Canvas footprint generated by
  brush.js for demonstrations and live input feeds retained writing opacity.
  The grayscale mask uses max/lighten composition to preserve faded timestamps
  on practice replay; fresh opacity matches the former 2.4-density brush.
- Added clearWriting to remove written pigment without clearing ambient ink;
  the writer restores accepted strokes within the current character/word.

dist/ink.js wraps this solver with slow autonomous ink emissions, pen-following
ink injection, visibility/reduced-motion handling, and a writable Canvas fallback
if floating-point WebGL is unavailable. The fallback is an approximation and
does not solve the fluid equations. Accessibility status is visually hidden.
Writing has a separate integrated fade clock; stamp inkTime values survive practice
restoration, clear operations do not reset the clock, and reduced-motion users
can enable opacity fading without restarting fluid movement. The Canvas history
flattens into a bounded raster checkpoint at its cap, preserving visible writing
instead of dropping old marks. All writing remains in page memory only.
The Canvas fallback uses a bounded, fading history of the same moving ambient
source, alongside the initial broad composition, without solving fluid physics.
